<thought>Based on the ESI‑MS spectrum the most intense ion is at m/z 224.1201, which corresponds to the protonated molecule [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the mass of a proton (1.007276 Da) gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 223.1128 Da. Searching for formulas that match this exact mass and show an M+1 intensity of ~17 % (consistent with ~15‑16 carbons) points to a composition containing 12 carbons, 15 hydrogens, 2 oxygens and one sulfur atom (C₁₂H₁₅O₂S). This formula fits the observed mass within a few ppm and the modest M+2 peak (~1.6 %) is compatible with the natural 34S isotope. Therefore the molecular formula of the sample compound is:</thought>
<final_answer>C12H15O2S</final_answer>
